candidates.title: US orders federal agencies to remove DeepSeek

articles.title: US orders federal agencies to remove China's DeepSeek AI from their systems

facts.fact: The Department of Homeland Security says federal civilian agencies must stop buying DeepSeek products and remove them from government IT systems over national security concerns.
The order also covers third-party products and services built with DeepSeek technology, though agencies can request exceptions.
DHS warned that sensitive data from U.S. government users could be reachable by Chinese authorities under Chinese law.
Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said Beijing opposes 'overstretching the concept of national security and politicizing technology and trade issues.'
A law passed in December 2025 already restricted DeepSeek in intelligence national security systems; the new order extends this to federal civilian agencies.
Bloomberg reported last week that China is considering export restrictions on 23 AI-related technologies, including chip designs and certain advanced AI models.
DeepSeek's R1 reasoning model shook the AI industry in January 2025, triggering a sharp sell-off in Nvidia shares.
A September report accused DeepSeek and five other Chinese AI companies, including Alibaba and Moonshot AI, of large-scale model distillation.

candidates.title: Meta's Muse app hits 10M US downloads in 40 days

articles.title: Meta's Muse hits 10M U.S. downloads in 40 days, a milestone reached by only 11 other apps

facts.fact: Muse had 10.9 million total downloads since its September debut, 10.2 million of them in the U.S., according to Sensor Tower.
Only 11 other apps have hit this post-launch milestone; the most recent was Meta's Threads in July 2023.
Disney+ is the only other non-game app in that group; the rest are mostly mobile games such as Fortnite, PUBG Mobile and Pokemon GO.
Meta put 39% of its total ad spend toward Muse in October, up from 23% the previous month.
Muse's U.S. 7-day retention was 30%, versus an average of 19% for rivals like ChatGPT, Claude and Grok.
Muse's daily active users reached 2.5 million on October 16, up 15% week over week.
ChatGPT had 3.7 million U.S. downloads in its first 40 days, versus 500,000 for Grok and 200,000 for Claude.
Muse is currently available only in the U.S. and Canada.

candidates.title: Amazon and Google go after Nvidia's software moat via PyTorch

articles.title: Google has joined Amazon in attacking Nvidia's stronghold with AI app developers

facts.fact: Google announced on Tuesday that TorchTPU, its version of PyTorch, is now open source.
Amazon made a similar announcement on Monday, releasing its own PyTorch version called TorchNeuron.
TorchNeuron lets AI apps move to Amazon's Trainium chip without rewriting them.
Amazon is also submitting code to the main PyTorch project so it works with hardware beyond Nvidia's chips by default.
PyTorch is used by about 85% of AI apps, according to some accounts.
Meta developed PyTorch in 2016 and handed it to the Linux Foundation in 2022.
Google says it worked with Meta, Hugging Face, Inferact (vLLM) and RadixArk (SGLang) on TorchTPU compatibility.

candidates.title: Anthropic and Nscale reportedly near another $45B compute deal

articles.title: Nscale and Anthropic are reportedly in talks for yet another $45B compute deal

facts.fact: Anthropic and Nscale announced a $45 billion compute deal a little over a month before this report.
Bloomberg reports the two are about to announce another $45 billion compute deal; talks are ongoing and terms could change.
A linked Information report refers to $517 billion in compute deals Anthropic struck within 11 months.
Some investors worry AI companies are spending heavily on compute for little profit.
Anthropic is still expected to go public in 2026.
Nscale is also pursuing an IPO, but Bloomberg reported on Oct 18 it faces investor pushback over a proposed $30 billion valuation.

candidates.title: Nvidia releases open Nemotron models for agents and AI PCs

articles.title: Nvidia launches new open models to run agents in the enterprise and on PCs
NVIDIA's new, open Nemotron 3.5 Super VL with post-training beats Claude Opus 5, GPT-6.1 Sol on specialized task benchmarks
articles.note: headline only, body not fetched; do not take facts from it

facts.fact: Nvidia launched Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, a 120-billion-parameter open-weight model for enterprise agents.
Nvidia says Super VL matches the instruction-following and tool-use accuracy of the larger Nemotron 3 Ultra with fewer parameters.
Two lightweight Bolt models target local use on AI PCs and workstations; Bolt 74B-A9B has 74 billion parameters.
The smallest model, Bolt E4B, targets conversational agents and arrives later this month.
Nvidia says companies using Super VL include Skydance, EY, Ramp, CrowdStrike, Perplexity and Salesforce.
Kari Briski, Nvidia VP of Open Models and Software, wrote that organizations can post-train Super VL on their own data, unlike closed frontier models.

candidates.title: Chip startup Tenstorrent raises $1.5B at $6.2B valuation

articles.title: Tenstorrent hits $6.2B valuation to scale open-weight AI chips

facts.fact: Tenstorrent, an inference-focused chip startup, raised $1.5 billion at a $6.2 billion valuation.
The valuation more than doubled the $2.6 billion it fetched in late 2024.
The round came five months after it reportedly drew acquisition interest from Intel and Qualcomm at valuations up to $5 billion.
Trace Capital and Innovation X led the round; backers include Cadence Ventures, Eclipse, Fidelity, SanDisk and T. Rowe Price.
CEO Jim Keller said the company stayed independent after its Galaxy servers showed they could run DeepSeek models.
Funds go toward scaling chips built for serving open-weight AI models and video generation.

candidates.title: Korean bookseller Kyobo rejects 100,000-book order over AI training fears

articles.title: Kyobo rejects suspicious 100,000-book order amid AI copyright fears

facts.fact: Kyobo Book Centre is Korea's largest bookstore operator.
A foreign company with no prior transaction history requested 100,000 books, one copy of every book regardless of subject.
Kyobo rejected the order because the buyer was not the 'end recipient'; the end recipient was identified only as a data company, citing contract terms.
The report links the concern to fears that bulk-bought books could be used as AI training data.
The Korean Publishers Association plans to survey major bookstores, secondhand booksellers and distributors about bulk-acquisition attempts.
The association plans to urge the government and National Assembly to strengthen book copyright legislation.

candidates.title: Microsoft and Korea's IITP send Korean AI students to Microsoft Research Asia

articles.title: Microsoft-IITP program helps Korean AI talents tap into global research resources

facts.fact: 31 master's and doctoral students worked with Microsoft Research Asia researchers in Beijing from March to September.
IITP has run the internship with Microsoft Research since 2011; more than 170 participants have completed it.
A Yonsei University Ph.D. student said interns could use nearly 100 GPUs, while a university lab researcher typically has about four.
Of the 170+ participants, 48 joined leading IT companies, 33 became university faculty and 25 joined AI research centers or public institutes.
Participants presented or published seven papers at leading international conferences in 2024 and eight in 2025.
